answer: A stake-bonded identity trellis makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a deposit as hard to fake as onyx, and the bond is slashed if the agent misbehaves. New identities start with no reputation, so they cannot harvest the nectar of rewards until they have done verifiable work over time. An attacker must therefore pay the full bond and waiting cost for every fake identity, turning a cheap flood into a linear, auditable expense.
